title: Circle and Rectangle Overlapping
summary: Given a circle defined by its radius and center coordinates, and an axis-aligned rectangle defined by its bottom-left and top-right corners, determine if there is any point that lies within both the circle and the rectangle.
statement: Given a circle defined by its radius and center coordinates, and an axis-aligned rectangle defined by its bottom-left and top-right corners, determine if there is any point that lies within both the circle and the rectangle.
constraints: The rectangle is axis-aligned with the two given opposite corners.
Touching at an edge or corner counts as overlap.
hints: Clamp the center to each rectangle coordinate range.
The clamped coordinates form the closest rectangle point.
Compare squared distance with squared radius, including equality.
Intersection exists exactly when this minimum distance is within the radius.
editorial: Intersection exists exactly when this minimum distance is within the radius.

tests.explanation: The circle touches the rectangle along x=1, so they overlap.
The nearest corner is farther than the radius.
